issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell specific land does not create a liability in that land that transfers to a replacement holding after consolidation, and loss of the land may make specific performance unavailable.
material_facts: The seller agreed to sell specified plots and received an advance.
The plots were affected by consolidation, after which the seller's rights in the original plots ceased and a new holding was allotted.
The buyer sought specific performance against the new holding, relying on the statutory transfer of liabilities to the new holding.
issues.conclusion: The agreement created no interest in or liability in the original holding that could transfer to the new holding. Because the seller's rights in the specified land ceased on consolidation, the agreement became void and could not be specifically enforced against the new holding.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, a contract for sale of immovable property does not of itself create an interest in or charge on the property. Section 55(1)(d) requires the seller to convey the property that is the subject of the contract, not different property. Under section 30(a) and (b) of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953, rights and liabilities in the original holdings cease and the tenure-holder has in the new holding the same rights and liabilities as in the original holdings; a sale agreement that created no interest or liability in the original land therefore gives rise to nothing transferable. When the specified property is lost through consolidation, the agreement becomes void under section 56 of the Contract Act. The Court approved Sugna v. Kali Ram and overruled Shanti Prasad v. Akhtar and Chetan Singh v. Hira Singh.

predicates.specific_performance_claim_concerns_land: A claimant sought specific performance of an agreement to sell land that was affected by a consolidation proceeding.
predicates.sale_agreement_created_no_interest_in_la: The agreement to sell the land did not itself create an interest in or charge on that land.
predicates.original_land_rights_ceased_under_consol: The seller's rights in the original land ceased when the seller entered into the replacement holding allotted through consolidation.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim concerns land removed by consolidation, the agreement created no interest in that land, and the seller's rights in it ceased, specific performance is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An advance paid under an agreement that cannot be specifically enforced may be ordered repaid when the seller agrees to repay it.
material_facts: The buyer pleaded that an advance had been paid under the agreement and sought its return as an alternative to specific performance.
The trial court found that the advance had been paid.
The seller stated in court that he was willing to repay the advance with interest.
issues.conclusion: The Court ordered the seller to repay the advance with interest.
issues.legal_principle: The Court ordered repayment on the basis of the established payment and the seller's stated willingness to refund it; it cited no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this order.

predicates.specific_performance_claim_includes_alte: A claimant seeking specific performance also sought repayment of the advance as an alternative remedy.
predicates.advance_was_paid: The claimant paid an advance to the seller under the agreement.
predicates.seller_agreed_to_repay: The seller stated that the seller was willing to repay the advance with interest.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim includes an alternative request for repayment, the advance was paid, and the seller agreed to repay it, repayment with interest is ordered.
